title: Orders service calls Billing for the user

story.title: You called the Orders service
story.what: Your token is scoped to the Orders service (aud=orders).
story.why: Each token is minted for one audience.
story.matters: Orders can't simply forward your token to Billing; Billing would reject the wrong audience.

story.title: Orders exchanged your token for one Billing will accept
story.what: Orders presented your token as subject_token and its own credentials as actor_token.
story.why: The authorization server decides if Orders may act for you at Billing.
story.matters: Delegation is explicit and policy-checked, not implicit token forwarding.

story.title: Billing saw both of you
story.what: The token's sub is you; its act.sub is the Orders service.
story.why: RFC 8693 records the delegation chain in the act claim.
story.matters: Billing can authorize and audit on both identities: who the charge is for, and which service asked.

subtitle: OAuth 2.0 Token Exchange (RFC 8693) with delegation

outcome.detail: Orders received a Billing-audience token that names both the user and itself.
outcome.caption: subject + actor exchanged · delegated token · Billing returned 201

tokens.label: Delegated token
tokens.note: Short-lived (5 minutes): exchanged tokens should be.
